task: W59 self-help action lifecycle review and isolated candidate
scope: No live helper or canvas edits; no browser, provider, native paint, renderer, or server calls

oracle.baseline: 5/12 passed; failures were pending/new source generation, same-path content replacement, in-place geometry move, duplicate ID with original object retained, absent ID, and in-place layer visibility change

changes: Action validity now records and rechecks committed source generation, readiness, path, and byte fingerprint. Pending or uncommitted source state cannot execute a chip.
A source API without the readiness contract does not grant a mutation; legacy tests with no source API retain prior behavior.

Zone actions require one nonempty stable ID, matching name, and unchanged compact geometry/mask stamp. Duplicate IDs and changed target geometry are refused; same-ID Undo clones and safe in-place reorder still work.
Layer visibility, opacity, blend, order, and lock state are included in the action stamp so in-place manual presentation changes stale a chip.
Controller confirmation rules and passive help behavior remain intact.

validation.w3_compatibility_replay: PASS 15/15 existing independent W3 review cases; replayed against the isolated candidate, not re-credited as fresh W59 evidence
validation.w4_compatibility_replay: PASS 12/12 existing independent W4 review cases and 8/8 semantic contract cases; replayed against the isolated candidate, not re-credited as fresh evidence

limits: The W53 source API candidate is not installed or live-accepted by this review; root owns any canvas integration.

The earlier active API snapshot lacks loading/committed-generation readiness fields. The W59 helper candidate therefore refuses mutations when an API exists without those fields. The W53 candidate supplies the required interface.
Zone mask validity uses a compact Adler checksum plus region descriptor data rather than a retained mask copy; this is bounded lifecycle protection, not a cryptographic identity proof.
The tests use the actual frozen helper bodies in a VM with controlled transaction and controller services; they do not exercise a browser UI or native canvas.
